terms.plain: The property tax rate. 1 mill = $1 of tax per $1,000 of taxable value.
Assessed value minus exemptions. Taxes are figured on this, not on market value.
The rate that would bring in the same tax money from existing property as last year. Above it is legally a tax increase, even if the rate itself didn't change.
The highest rate a board can adopt; set in July and printed on the TRIM notice. It can go down later, not up.
Truth in Millage notice mailed in August showing each government's proposed tax and hearing dates.
The main operating budget: police, parks, administration. Most property tax goes here.
Business-like services paid by user fees, such as water, sewer and garbage.
Big one-time building and infrastructure spending.
Savings carried forward for emergencies and stability.
Money left over from last year that is budgeted again this year.
Elected offices funded through the county: Sheriff, Clerk, Property Appraiser, Tax Collector, Supervisor of Elections.
Community Redevelopment Agency: an area where growth in property taxes is set aside for local improvements.
The school tax rate set by the state, not the School Board.
A mid-year change to the adopted budget. Florida cities must post them online within 5 days.
Reduces taxable value of a primary home. Currently $25,000 for all taxes plus another $25,000 for non-school taxes on value over $50,000.
Voter-approved change raising the non-school homestead exemption to $150,000 in 2027 and $250,000 in 2028.
